I am a Principal Economist at the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System and previously served as an economist at the Federal Trade Commission and the Department of Justice Antitrust Division. My research and software develop practical tools for antitrust and competition policy, with a focus on merger review, market definition, merger simulation, model choice, efficiencies, financial structure, and the use of economic evidence under uncertainty.

Across nearly two decades of public service, I have led economic investigations and supported high-profile litigations involving retail banking, semiconductors, health insurance, cinema and radio advertising, airlines, and parking services. That experience informs a broader research agenda on how agencies, courts, and practitioners should use economic models when the evidence is informative but incomplete, including in banking, which has been central to U.S. merger law since *Philadelphia National Bank* and offers unusually rich public data for studying merger effects.
